evidence.locator: German Art. 15 first sentence; English Art. 15 first paragraph
evidence.verified: The parties share statements about both kinds, the sacrament of Christ's true body and blood, and spiritual receiving; a summary of Article 15 as complete disagreement is wrong.
evidence.limit: No witness collation or doctrinal adjudication; historical spelling is from the edited German source.

evidence.locator: German Art. 15 closing paragraph, English corresponding final sentence
evidence.verified: The precisely recorded nonagreement concerns whether Christ's true body and blood are corporeally present in bread and wine, not whether any kind of communion is acknowledged.
evidence.limit: Avoid back-projecting a fully settled later technical confessional vocabulary or the statement that all participants viewed the Supper as symbolic.

evidence.verified: The collection differentiates presentation on June 25 from itemized 1530 German and Latin printed editions and notes unreliable early unauthorized printed versions.
evidence.limit: Do not infer manuscript identity, exact submitted copy, or complete exhaustive edition list from this webpage alone.

evidence.verified: Gruber 46 records a Latin Confession plus Apology printed at Wittenberg by Georg Rhau, dated 1531.
evidence.limit: The catalogue says 'first Latin edition' according to a note inside the front cover; the note is evidence of catalogued attribution, not an independently verified first-edition census.

evidence.verified: The catalogue identifies a spring 1531 Latin authorized text and Apology under Melanchthon's supervision; despite bilingual cover information, its described content is only Latin.
evidence.limit: A title-page claim that an object contains German and Latin is not proof the specific described copy includes both.

evidence.verified: Gruber 7 is described as German Confession and Apology translated by Justus Jonas with a November 1531 colophon. Gruber 43 and 62 concern German versions, but 62 has an uncertain handwritten Luther provenance note.
evidence.limit: Do not label Gruber 7 as printed in Augsburg based solely on its title's references to the 1530 Augsburg Diet; its described colophon confirms a date, not here the printing location.

evidence.locator: Gruber 28 title and paragraph immediately below
evidence.verified: Gruber 28 is described as a 1540 Latin Augsburg Confession and Apology from Wittenberg, identified by the cataloguer as Variata.
evidence.limit: This does not establish that every 1540 printing is Variata or constitute complete collation of Article X and all copies.

evidence.locator: Gruber 28 and Pitts image-details book title
anchorTokens: Addita est Apologia Confessionis diligenter recognita
evidence.verified: The title's feminine participle recognita grammatically modifies Apologia, not Confessio. The publisher's description separately labels the 1540 Confession as Variata.
evidence.limit: Do not claim that recognita on the title page alone states the Augsburg Confession was revised; source descriptions and actual Article X readings must be kept separate.

evidence.locator: Gruber 28 Art. X paraphrase; Schaff 1530/1540 paired readings
anchorTokens: cum pane et vino vere exhibeantur
evidence.verified: The cited historical comparison reports that Article X's 1530/1531 language of true presence and distribution is differently formulated in 1540 as true exhibition with bread and wine; the explicit disapproval clause is not retained.
evidence.limit: This is a limited phrase comparison mediated by later editions, not an autopsy-based transcription of both unique surviving 16th-century exemplars. Theological intent and all version boundaries remain expert questions.

evidence.locator: Unnumbered paragraph between Gruber 28 and Saxon confession
evidence.verified: The catalogue describes an Augsburg Confession plus Apology copy dated 1540 which it explicitly says is not Variata, and gives Nils Forsander provenance.
evidence.limit: An individual Gruber inventory number, imprint transcription, signatures and a demonstrable textual side-by-side comparison are absent from that paragraph; no identifier should be invented.

evidence.locator: Emory Pitts digital object ID 6759 and Gruber 28 item
evidence.verified: Pitts independently documents and identifies a 1540 altered edition image, supporting existence of another institutional 1540 Variata witness; two descriptions do not prove identity of their physical copies.
evidence.limit: Pitts public-domain rights notice is institution-qualified; do not copy the archive image into the app without a separately recorded asset decision.

evidence.locator: GHDI bibliography and English translator credit; Gruber object notes; Pitts digitized title-page description
evidence.verified: Distinct roles of original-language edited transcription, translation, object-catalogue descriptions and university digitized object description can be traced.
evidence.limit: These sources are not interchangeable with a facsimile autopsy or critical original-copy stemma.

evidence.locator: Bente's reception-history paragraphs; Pitts editorial statement on Lutheran Church confessional use
evidence.verified: Later confessional historiography records eventual preference for the unaltered confession in Lutheran confession-making.
evidence.limit: Neither source establishes universal reception across all churches, readers, dates, territories or actual Melanchthon intention. Bente's confessional judgments should not become neutral facts.

evidence.locator: Gruber 28 characterizes Melanchthon's motivations as compromise with Calvinists; older confessional and historical accounts differ
evidence.verified: The 'compromise with Calvinists' phrasing is the cataloguer's modern interpretation, not a literal statement proven to occur in the 1540 title page or the Article X Latin quotation.
evidence.limit: No conclusion about author's motivation, anachronism in all uses of the term, or 1540 actors' self-naming follows from this wording alone. Require modern neutral historiography and contemporary correspondence.
